facts.say: Smoke masks our alarm smell and makes us fill up on honey, so we calm down.
Nobody is sure why smoke makes bees gorge. One idea is that we get ready to flee a fire.
Our alarm smell is a chemical that also smells like bananas.
A crushed bee gives off alarm smell, and that calls more guards.
Beekeepers lift the hive to check its food. A light hive is a hungry hive.
Feed bees sugar syrup, never store honey: it can carry foulbrood spores.
Foulbrood spores last for decades, and the disease kills bee larvae.
Foulbrood is harmless to people, and the honey is still safe to eat.
A smaller hive entrance needs fewer guards to defend it.
Yellowjackets follow sweet smells like syrup, and they also eat lots of pest insects.
Bees can't swim. They need pebbles or a landing spot to drink from.
Bees cool the hive by spreading water drops and fanning their wings.
The brood nest is kept at about thirty-five degrees Celsius.
Drones are the male bees. No stinger, no pollen baskets, no wax glands, and they don't forage.
Drones get pushed out of the hive in fall.
A stinger is a modified egg-laying tube, so only female bees can sting.
Worker bees are all female.
The queen lays the colony's eggs. She's the only bee in the hive that does.
Undertaker bees carry dead bees out of the hive.
Festooning is bees hooking their legs together into chains. Nobody is sure why.
Calm swarms are usually gentle and rarely sting.
In winter the bees huddle around the queen and shiver to keep warm.
Hardly any bees forage in the rain.
Bees can't see red, but they can see ultraviolet light.
Japanese honeybees ball around a giant hornet and heat it to about forty-six degrees Celsius.
There are over twenty thousand kinds of bee, and about four thousand are native to the US.
About seven in ten wild bees nest in the ground. A patch of bare dirt helps.
Honey bees are livestock, kept by beekeepers. Wild bees have no keeper; they need habitat.
US beekeepers lost more than half their managed colonies in one recent year.
Varroa mites and the viruses they spread are a big reason hives die.
Bees carry pesticide home in pollen and nectar, right to the babies.
Plant native flowers that bloom from spring to fall, and skip the bug spray. A balcony pot counts.
About three in four leading food crop types benefit from pollinators. Grains like wheat don't need them.
The rusty patched bumble bee is down about eighty-seven percent, the first bumble bee on the endangered list.
Bees don't stop fires, but they help burned land grow back.
After one Oregon wildfire, the most burned spots had about twenty times more wild bees.
Pollinators usually bounce back after one fire, but fires that come too often hurt them.
Beeswax is a stingerless drone and shop steward of Local Twenty Thousand, the union for every kind of bee.
Honeymoon One is the humans' evacuation rocket. Beeswax rode it to the Moon himself.
From the Moon, Earth barely moves in the sky. It just hangs there.
Earth is the only place we've ever found flowers.

dont_say: bees prevent, stop or reduce wildfires
smoke makes bees think there's a fire (it is only one idea)
the rusty patched was the first bee listed (it was the first BUMBLE bee)
hold out your hand to bees
